page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-2 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the n4 server family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel core with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The underlying Intel processor includes an L3 cache of 260 MB, L2 cache of 2 MB, and L1d cache of 48 KB, alongside hardware support for advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions.

Benchmark evaluations indicate a clear performance asymmetry between single-core and multi-core workloads. Single-core execution is moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the average tier. Similarly, single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression demonstrate average throughput. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations show significant limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU score fall into the poor tier. Memory subsystem performance is also constrained, with read-only large block bandwidth and write large block bandwidth both ranking in the bottom 10% of tested configurations.

Given the hardware profile and benchmark results, this instance is positioned as an entry-level general-purpose node. It exhibits weak performance in complex tasks such as software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations, which score in the bottom 10% to 25% tiers. LLM inference speeds are also low, with a small 135M model achieving weak tokens-per-second throughput. Consequently, the n4-standard-2 is suited for lightweight, non-intensive workloads such as basic web serving, text processing, and simple utility scripting. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, it offers a low-cost entry point into the dedicated Intel architecture with modern instruction sets, though it presents a clear tradeoff in multi-threaded scaling and memory throughput.

Lacking local storage and GPU accelerators, it relies on an Intel processor equipped with a 260 MB L3 cache and advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct contrast: single-core CPU execution and single-threaded compression tasks rank in the average tier, whereas multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth fall into the bottom 10% of tested systems. Similarly, software compilation, database operations, and LLM inference show weak to poor throughput. This resource profile makes the instance qualitatively cost-effective for low-intensity, single-threaded applications, basic text processing, and lightweight web serving, while presenting clear performance tradeoffs for memory-intensive or highly parallelized workloads.
